Hey everyone.

So I have noticed that it is not uncommon here for people to crosspost the same article across 4+ subreddits all at the same time.

I feel like one of the vibes I have been getting from Voat since I joined is a focus on quality discussions and I can't help but think that cross-posting the same link/article to 4 different places, and thus initiating 4 different conversations in different places is counter to the idea of fostering quality discussions.

I am not sure what the best solution is but there has got to be something better than current practices.

What if any time someone posts a link it gets "claimed" by the first sub its posted to and then any other submissions create a new post in whatever other subreddits it's posted to but its the same comment thread across all instances.

Like I said, I'm not sure what the best solution is but there has got to be something that can be done on the server side to consolidate.
CrossPosting: There has got to be a better way
I was thinking that maybe we could tag a certain amount of relevant subs that all lead to the same discussion. Most things fit in several different categories.
I agree with having crossposts point to a single comment thread.

Yea. Like I said in the OP. I can not decide what I think is the best solution because even for this I can see examples of where it would cause problems.

For example, there are some more academic focused subs popping up, the discussion in those is going to be slightly different than the discussion in /v/news

Plus certain subs are going to have different criteria for moderating discussions, which raises a whole other issue with how these merged discussion threads will get moderated and who is in charge of them.

Further, there are issues with the same "story" being on a dozen different websites.

Maybe a means of combining them all into a single point for which the discussion springs from? The issue is how to integrate things and so on, especially on the fly where someone might post the original press release, and then 5 people merge new stories to that press releases post, and then someone else posts it again 40 min later and no one notices its the same thing as the other combined thread until a discussion has already started.

I am SURE there is a way to do something awesome here, and I see it as a real opportunity to set Voat apart from other news aggregate sites, but its going to be a tough nut to crack if this direction is decided to be one worth exploring.

I think the best solution would be to create a single comment thread and have it linked to in multiple subs. This is done sometimes by the submitters, but it should be done automatically as a feature of Voat. It would greatly simplify cross-sub discussions. I think it would make sense to treat crossposts as separate from normal posts. Not sure exactly how they should be differentiated, but that would make the most sense. I guess one obvious way they would be different is that cross-posts is that the subverse sidebar/stylesheet/name doesn't exist when viewing a crosspost. I'm not sure how moderation would be handled though, as it would be in multiple subs with different rules. Maybe each sub's moderators would be able to hide a crossposted thread or comments in the thread for their specific subverse, but none of the mods for any given sub that a thread was posted in could delete anything.

Just my thoughts on the subject. I definitely think there is a lot of potential in how Voat handles crossposts, but it will be difficult to decide exactly what should be done.

I think this would be nice, but I don't believe that it is ideal. I say this because in my experience on reddit, different subreddits - and i assume different subverses in the future - will have varying approaches to topics. /r/infp may approach the comments on an article in a very different way than people in /r/conspiratard, and allowing the communities with their respective cultures to have a space to discuss the articles in their own ways is desirable to me.

I think that it could be good to have the option to view a combined comment page, which merges all of the discussions for a link into a single view - while by default letting you see just the comments for the post on the subverse you opened it on.

That said, comments on articles on reddit for example can become quite unwieldy. I often don't read 95% of the comments on an article after viewing a few of the top rated or newest ones when there are thousands of them on a single page. I think this speaks to another need for a more streamlined less redundant method of online discourse, but that's beyond the scope of this discussion.

Maybe give people the option to customize which posts to include or not include in their view of the merged comments page, so you could for instance exclude comments from something like /v/onlystupidcomments from the combined view.

So that would resolve the discussion being fragmented too much. It does not yet resolve the problem of the appearance of spam. If I am subscribed to multiple subverses where the article is cross-posted to, then i have the same headline appearing two, three, or more times on my front page. Worse, if I am browsing /v/all then I may see the same article many times, occupying space that could be used for other things I am interested in.

So the simple solution here is to make this a per-user thing. If the same article is posted to multiple subverses in a particular view (i.e. viewing a personalized front page, or viewing /v/all), then hide the lower ranking ones, show only the top-scoring one. When the user clicks on a vote arrow, give them the option to select which of the different posts to vote on.

So now if you visit each of those subverses individually directly, you will still see the same cross-posted article on each, but if you are viewing /v/all or your personalized front page then you will only see it in one spot on the list.

Now the next problem is re-posts. Sometimes it is appropriate to post a link to the same article multiple times on the same subverse. Perhaps after an interval has passed and more information has come about, or when someone desires a fresh conversation on the subject. Or maybe if the original post did not get the visibility that is really deserved (which is a whole other can of worms that may be beyond the scope of this discussion - or maybe it really is at the heart of this, I'm not sure). So in these instances, favor the most recent and highest scoring posts in determining where the post is visible on any given view that has multiple copies of the same article. If it's been a year since an article was linked, then when it gets reposted, treat it as normal. But still allow the ability to view merged comments, so you can see what the old discussion on the matter was, and differentiate it from current discussion.

This situation requires some careful thought about archival, and about building on past reflections on content rather than repeating it. I disagree with reddit's archival policy or preventing discussion on any comments older than 6 months, but i recognize some of the motivations behind it as warranting attention.

anyway, i think this would be a pretty decent interim solution.

This is one of those issues that I feel needs a community solution, rather than an admin based or server-side thing. Any duplicate link posted anywhere site-wide should be met with a warning saying as much. I don't really see how duplicate links posted to multiple subs is anything other than spam. This is different from a cross post with an internal link, linking to the original submission['s comment thread] because if you think about it, it's very likely that the users in /v/phdastrophysics are going to have a different discussion from /v/spacepix. I think two such communities should be allowed, perhaps even encouraged, to have their respective discussions.

Perhaps that could be solved with a checkbox that defaults as cross-sub vs. local sub for comments; unchecking the box when submitting could essentially spawn a subverse specific discussion if people wanted. This would of course require having the sub you found the link in as a variable. This would also keep the conversations linked for those interested in reviewing both.

I think that comment threads already allow for this, though. Voat is relatively small - no one is wading through thousands of repeat comments (yet). Users from different verses could discuss in threads that interest them, but they'd also be exposed to different perspectives - which, to me, is pretty cool.

It sort of just depends on what direction we want to go in as users, I guess.

I disagree about it being spam. Not everyone may subscribe to the same subverses, so if an article is relevant to /v/technology as well as /v/music for example, the people who subscribe to one but not the other might miss out on something relevant to their interests if it were not cross-posted.

I can agree that it would take on the functionality of spam for people who are subscribed to the different subverses where it is cross-posted, and I don't think that that is the only way in which cross-posting manifests.

I mean, it's either spam or it isn't. It's pretty hard to say that posting the same link over and over is not spam. I don't see the issue with cross-posting into the second sub with an internal link to the first post, rather than the same external link repeatedly. Never mind that it makes /v/all pretty hard to read at times.

Maybe the source of our disagreement is a variation in our respective definitions of spam? I suppose that I define spam in the context of a website like this as repeated postings of the same content, or a variation of that content, in a way that is disruptive to an individual's or group's experience of the site. If that content is not disruptive, then it is not at that time spam.

What may be disruptive to one person's experience of the site may not be disruptive to another person's. So yes, I can acknowledge that if you see the same content posted repeatedly while viewing /v/all or your front page, then for your experience it is spam. And for those who do not browse /v/all or who only subscribe to one of the subverses the content is posted to, it is not spam.

Apart from the question of whether it is spam or not, is the question of cost versus benefit.

Who benefits from cross-posting?

Is the cost of some seeing repeated postings of the same content in their experience on the site greater or less than the benefit of those who see it only once? Or put another way, is the cost of some seeing repeated postings of the same content greater than the cost of some never seeing it at all?

I don't like spam either. I'm not saying that we should not worry about the problem - it IS a problem.

I suppose my concern here really is a universal mis-attribution of intention. Some people who cross-post may be doing so in order to collect points or to force their content on people who really don't want to see it. I think this is bad. Some people who cross-post may be doing it in order to make sure that relevant content is shared with those who may be interested in it. I think this is good.

When we call all cross-posting spam, we may fall into the trap of ignoring the motivations of the latter case, the problem that the cross-posting is attempting to remedy in those instances.

Then again maybe I'm misunderstanding totally. :s If so, I apologize.
